FOREWORD This Indian Standard ( Part 4 ) ( First Revision ) was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards on 5 May 1989, after the draft finalized by the Methods of Test for Petroleum, Petroleum Products and Lubricants Sectional Committee had been approved by the Petroleum, Coal and Related Products Division Council.

PART 4 SAMPLING OF PETROLEUM ( COKE FOR LABORATORY ANALYSIS

in a lot ( shipment ) of raw p:troleum coke. The gross sample and all R.P.`s of the gross sample used to obtainthe analytical moisture sample shall be protected from changes in composition due to exposure to rain, snow, wind, sun, contact with absorbent materials, and extremes of temperature ( not less than ambient climate or greater than 45�C ). The circulation of air through equipment shall be reduced to a minimum. Samples in which moisture content is important shall be protected from excessive air flow and then shall be stored in moisture tight containers. 3 COLLECTION OF GROSS SAMPLE 3.1 Sample coke while it is being loaded into or unloaded from railroad cars, ships or trucks or when discharged from supply bins, belt conveyors or other coke conveying equipment. Mechanical sample devices are more reliable than taking the sample `by hand. However, when it is not possible, hand sampling may be done. Sample is close to the point of interest as possible. 3.2 When taking the sample, use a pail or a specially built receptacle which may be swung completely across the following stream in a brief interval, so as to take all of the stream for a fixed interval. Under no circumstances should the sampling receptacle be allowed to overflow or spill. 3.3 Increments should be collected regularly and systematically and with such frequency, so that the entire quantity of the coke sampled shall be proportionately represented in the gross sample. The standard gross sample should approach the quantities given in Table 1. Table 1 Mass of the Gross Sample for Tonne of Coke
Minimum Sample Required Gross Sample

Adapted with permission from ASTM D 316-78 and ASTM D 2013-86 1 SCOPE 1.1 This standard ( Part 4 ) describes a procedure for the collection and preparation of petroleum coke samples for laboratory analysis. 2 TERMINOLOGY 2.1 Gross Samples The original sample representing one lot of petroleum coke, that is, composed of a number of increments on which size reduction or division has not been performed. 2.2 Bulk Samples A representative portion ( R.P. ) of the gross sample prepared for ease of handling. When.the gross sample is very large it is desirable to have practical amounts to handle for further subdivision of the R.P. The bulk sample should not be greater than about 90 kg. and should be no less than about 25 kg. If the gross sample is less than about 90 kg. a bulk sample is not needed. 2.3 Analytical Sample The quantity of petroleum coke sample delivered to the laboratory for further preparation and analysis of a small R.P. of the gross sample or bulk sample specifically designed for a particular analytical test. 2.4 Sub-sample An unbiased portion taken from the sample at any point during sample reduction or division, or both, to be used for a special purpose. 2.5 Description of Riffle Divider A manual sample divider which divides the sample of petroleum coke into two parts of approximately equal mass. Typical riffle bucket and riffle stands are shown in Fig. 1. 2.5.1 It is preferable that feed chutes and enclosed riffles are used for sample preparation. The slope of feed chutes and riffles shall be at least 60 degree for free flow of moist material. 2.6 Air-Drying A process of partial drying of coke to bring its moisture near to equilibrium with the atmosphere in the room in which further reduction and division of the sample is to take place. 2.7 Moisture Sample A representative portion ( R.P. ) of the gross sample used to check the `As reczivzd moisture 1

5 PREPARATION OF COKE SAMPLE FOR LABORATORY ANALYSIS 5.1 Gross Sample 5.1.1

The preparation of the gross sample shall be done by trained and experienced personnel and should be performed in an enclosed space, roofed, cool and free from excessive air movements. 5.1.2 In handling the gross sample the entire quantity of petroleum coke thus being sampled should be represented proportionately in the subsample. 5.2 `As Received' Moisture for Raw Coke ) Sample ( Applicable

of 10 to 15�C above room temperature, with a maximum temperature of 45�C. Air volume changes should be at the rate of 1 to 4 per minutes to avoid excessive drying. A typical oven is shown in Fig. 3.

5.2.1 If a moisture sample is needed for a lot ( shipment > of raw petroleum coke for determinatlon of moisture on `As Received' basis, representative portion of about 2.5 kg is taken from the gross sample before air-drying, by the use of a riffle ( 75 mm riffle ). 5.2.2 Crush the moisture sample rapidly to below 12'5 mm and determine the moisture content ( `As Received' by Method A-l ). 5.2.3 When the gross sample contains excessive moisture which will hamper the riffling operation for the moisture R.P., the gross sample shall be weighed and air dried and weighed again recording the percent, mass loss. The moisture R.P. sample ( 2.5 kg ) is now riffled from the gross 5.2.2. The sample and processed following moisture content of the lot `As Received' ( shipment ) of raw coke will consist of the percent mass loss ( moisture ) on air-drying plus the percent mass loss ( Method A-l ). 5.2.4 For air-drying the gross sample the following methods is suitable. either of

5.2.4.1 Drying pans may be used of non-corroding metal of sufficient size so that the sample may be spread to a depth of preferably not more than 25 mm with sides of the pan not more than 38 mm high. The room should be free of dust and excessive air currents in order to avoid contamination. 5.2.4.2 Air-drying ovens may be used to pass slightly heated air over the sample. The oven should be capable of maintaining a temperature 3

FIG. 3 AIR-DRYING OVEN 5.2.4.3 A drying floor may be used to dry the gross sample. A smooth clean floor in a room free from dust and excessive air current is suitable. 5.2.4.4 Continue air-drying until the loss in mass of the total gross sample is not more than

IS 1447 ( Psrt 4 > : 1989 0.1 percent per hour. Stirring at intervals will lessen air-drying time. Avoid excessive drying time. 5.3 Bulk Sample 5.3.1 The gross sample is now sub-divided to yield a bulk sample for convenience in handling and for ultimately making the small analytical sample required. To obtain a bulk sample from a large gross sample, the top size particle shall be no larger than the particle size listed in Table 2 below for the mass of the gross sample. 5.3.8 The gross sample is now reduced to a bulk sample that may be conveniently handled. The bulk sample is now ready for the small analytical sample. 5.4 Analytical Sample 5.4.1 The bulk sample is now handled in a way depending upon whether it is calcined or raw petroleum coke, to obtain the analytical sample. Two general schematics ( I and II ) are given below, one for raw petroleum coke and the other for calcined petroleum coke for the reduction of the bulk sample to any specific size portion analytical sample.

5.3.2

The bulk sample need not be greater than about 90 kg and should be no less than 25 kg. If the gross sample is to be further subdivided to obtain a bulk sample, this may be done by employing a mechanical sample reducer. 5.3.3 The desired bulk sample may also be obtained by using a riffle after the gross sample has been sized to meet the requirement in Table 2. 5.3.4 Air dry ( see 5.2.4 ) the gross sample, if needed, so that it may _be fed properly through the large riffle ( 75 mm riffle ). Calcined coke usually do not require air-drying. 5.3.5 Reduce the gross sample to a top size to meet the requirement in Table 2. 5.3.6 Determine the number of passes required in the riffling operation from the total mass of the gross sample and the mass desired for the bulk sample. 5.3.7 Pass the coke through the riffle from a feed scoop, feed bucket or riffle pan having a lip or opening the full length of the riffle. When using any of the above containers to feed the riffle, spread the coke evenly in the container, raise the container, and hold it with its front edge resting on the top of the feed through, then slowly tilt it so that the coke flows in a uniform stream through the hopper straight down over the centre of riffle into each and all the slots, then ,into the pans. Under no circumstances shovel the sample into the riffle or dribble into the riffle from a small mouthed container. Do not allow the coke to build up in or above the riffle slots. If it does not flow freely through the slots, shake or vibrate the riffle to facilitate the flow. The riflle used for the above operation shall have a slot opening of at least 2 to 24 times greater than the top size particle of the petroleum coke being riffled. 4

5.4.2.4 Using a riffle, split the bulk sample to obtain a 700 g portion. Follow the procedure for riffling mentioned in 5.3.6 and 5.3.7. 5.4.2.5 Grind the 700 g sub-sample to pass a 3'35 mm sieve using a roll crusher. Do not overgrind. Riffle the sample to about 350 g. 5.4.2.6 Using a roll crusher grind 350 g of sub-sample to pass through 250-micron IS Sieve. Do not overgrind. About one half of the sample at this point should be retained on a 125-micron IS Sieve. 5.4.2.7 Dry the 350 g sample (as obtained in 5.4.2.6 ) to constant mass at 95" to 105�C. This dried sample is now ready for analysis of ( see Method A-2 ) volatile matter, moisture ash content and other chemical analysis. The dried sample may be stored in a closed container within a desiccator. Thoroughly mix the sample before extracting portion for analysis. 5.4.3 Analytical Sample from a Bulk Sample of
Calcined Petroleum Coke

depending upon the coke and the mass of the gross sample from which the bulk sample came. 5.4.3.2 The bulk sample is to be air-dried if necessary in accordance with 5.2.4. Very seldom does a calcined coke has to be air dried. 5.4.3.3 The bulk sample of calcined petroleum coke is ground according to the mass and size indicated in Table 2 and is riffled into an approximately 2'5 kg portion. 5.4.3.4 The 2'5 kg portion of the bulk sample is now ground to pass 6'7 mm sieve using a jaw crusher ( do not overgrind ) and is riffled into approximately 1'8 kg. 5.4.3.5 The 1'8 kg riffled portion of minus ( - ) 6'7 mm sample is further ground in a roll crusher to pass 850-micron IS Sieve. Do not overgrind the sample. Divide the sample to obtain about 500 g. 5.4.3.6 Grind this 500 g sub-sample with a roll crusher to pass through 250-micron IS Sieve and divide into two parts. 5.4.3.7 The first portion ( 250 g ) of sample is used for the analytical sample for moisture 5

5.4.3.1 The bulk sample of calcined coke will vary in mass from 25 kg to about 90 kg and will vary in top size particle from 6 mm to 38 mm

IS 1447 ( Part 4 ) : 1989 ( see Method A-2 ), volatile matter, ash, sulphur, silicon and trace metal analysis. 5.4.3.8 The second portion ( 250 g ) of the sample is further ground to 150 micron size and about 35 g portion riffled out and ground in a ball mill or other suitable pulverizing equipment to pass through 75-micron IS Sieve. This sample is used as the analytical sample for real density test. 5.4.3.9 Store sample in closed containers and mix thoroughly before extracting portions for analysis. 5.5 Operation of Grinding Equipment 5.5.1 Jaw Crusher Operation a) Every effort should be made to grind a sample in such a manner so that contaminants are not introduced into the sample. The jaw crusher should be cleaned after each use; b) Set the jaw crusher to the top size particle desired by using the manganese steel jaw plates; 4 Pass only + ( mesh ) sample through the jaw crusher catching the sample below the jaw in a suitable container; slowly, never 4 Feed the jaw crusher completely filling or overflowing the jaw compartment.
b) 5.5.2 4 Roll Crusher Operation

c>

4

e)

Every effort should be made to grind a sample in such a manner that contaminants are not introduced into the sample. It is a good practice to avoid the same sample preparation equipment for handling both types of petroleum cokes ( calcined and raw ). In grinding a coke, set the rolls far enough apart to crush only the largest particles of sample ( R.P. ). Screen out all the minus ( - ) mesh of the size ( particle ) desired, commonly known as scalping. Only the plus ( + ) mesh is to be crushed again. Turn the roll crusher on and pour the scalped sample very slowly through the rolls. Again scalp off the plus ( + ) mesh size and blend of the minus ( - ) size with the minus ( - ) mesh size in ( c > above. Only the plus ( + ) mesh size is to be ground through the roll crusher again. The crushing and scalping of the material is repeated until all the material is in the minus ( - ) mesh desired. Make sure the final minus ( - ) mesh particles are blended well. Do not rush the above operation.
